clue.text: Food for a solitary sailor?

blocks.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is the usual crossword sailor
solitary means on your own

explanation.surface: What a lone seaman eats on a long voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'solitary sailor' as a sailor who is on his own: the sailor comes first, then the description.
explanation.definitionFit: Abalone is an edible sea snail, a shellfish eaten as a delicacy.

clue.text: Receive Church of England priest? Indeed!

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for the Church of England
P is a dictionary abbreviation for priest
read as 'in deed': a deed is an act, and the 'in' places the other pieces inside it

explanation.surface: A surprised question: is an Anglican priest really to be welcomed?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indeed!' looks like an exclamation of emphasis, but it splits as 'in deed', which both supplies the outer word and says the other pieces go inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To accept something is to take or receive it when offered.

clue.text: Devotee, to sum up, gets caught in it

indicators.note: something caught in something else is held inside it

blocks.note: to add is to sum numbers up
taken as written; it is split open for the insertion
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A fan, in short, becomes trapped by the thing they love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caught' does double duty: it supplies the cricket abbreviation and, with 'gets ... in', says where that letter goes.
explanation.definitionFit: An addict is an enthusiast hooked on something, a devoted fan.

clue.text: Takes the corner badly and reverses to crash

indicators.note: a crash leaves things smashed and jumbled, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: the letters of these two words are the fodder

explanation.surface: A bad driver misjudges a bend, backs up, then hits something.
explanation.definitionFit: A car that oversteers turns more sharply than the driver intends, a classic way to mishandle a bend.

clue.text: Strive to get second opinion out of specialist

indicators.note: second points to the letter in position two of the following word
taking something out of a word removes it from that word

blocks.note: a specialist is an expert
the second letter of opinion

explanation.surface: Trying hard to obtain another doctor's view from a consultant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second opinion' sounds like a medical phrase, but it just means the second letter of 'opinion', removed from EXPERT.
explanation.definitionFit: To exert yourself is to make a strenuous effort, which is to strive.

clue.text: TV prompt to report traffic jam?

indicators.note: a report is spoken out, so the words are judged by their sound

blocks.note: a traffic jam is a queue of cars, or autos

explanation.surface: A newsreader's prompter set up for reading out the traffic news.
explanation.walkthrough: Auto is American and old-fashioned for a car, so a queue of autos is a traffic jam.
explanation.definitionFit: An Autocue is the screen that scrolls a script for television presenters to read.

clue.text: A lot of trees cut back with help, as previously mentioned

indicators.note: cutting something at the back trims off its final letter

blocks.note: taken as written
a forest is a large area of trees
aid is help

explanation.surface: Pruning a woodland with assistance, as already described.
explanation.walkthrough: A FOREST loses its last letter, then AID is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Aforesaid is a formal, legal-sounding word for things mentioned earlier in a text.

clue.text: Old City conservative has a change of heart

indicators.note: the heart is the middle of a word, and changing it here means rearranging those central letters

blocks.note: a Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A Conservative from the City of London changes his mind.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the two middle letters of TORY swap places.
explanation.definitionFit: Troy is the ancient city besieged by the Greeks in Homer's Iliad.

clue.text: A number claim it is changeable, like the weather

indicators.note: changeable things can take a different form, so the letters can be put in another order

blocks.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100
taken as written, letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Several people say something is as unpredictable as the weather.
explanation.walkthrough: The C from 'A number' joins the anagram fodder; both Cs are shuffled with the letters of 'claim it'.
explanation.definitionFit: Climatic means relating to climate, the long-run pattern of weather.

clue.text: Set off, wander about and separate

indicators.note: something off is out of its normal state, so these letters are disordered

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
to range is to roam or wander

explanation.surface: Instructions to leave, roam around and part company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set off' looks like 'depart' but is an anagram of SET; 'wander about' reads naturally together, though 'about' is just filler here.
explanation.definitionFit: To estrange people is to drive them apart, making them separate.

clue.text: Seek favour for daughter in prison

indicators.note: placed in something means set inside it

blocks.note: D is the standard abbreviation for daughter
a cage is a place of confinement

explanation.surface: A parent pleads for leniency for a jailed daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seek favour' is a loose definition: to cadge is to ask for something free.
explanation.definitionFit: To cadge is to beg or scrounge, asking someone for a free favour.

clue.text: European Community has no record on first green expert

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
nothing, zero, the letter O
a log is a written record
1st with the number written as I

explanation.surface: A complaint that Brussels keeps no account of being first in environmental matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First' is read as 1ST, with the 1 as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: An ecologist studies the environment, and green means environmentally minded.

clue.text: Quiet one with dog is leader of the pack

blocks.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet
an ace is the one in a pack of cards
a setter is a breed of gundog

explanation.surface: A calm owner with a dog that heads the pack of hounds.
explanation.walkthrough: The pack and the dog suggest hounds; the definition means the runner who sets the speed.
explanation.definitionFit: A pacesetter leads the field and sets the speed, so is out in front of the rest.

clue.text: Story of how silver was found in it

indicators.note: something found in something else sits inside it

blocks.note: it is crossword slang for sex appeal, SA
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: The tale of a silver strike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' meaning sex appeal comes from the 1920s 'It girl'; crosswords use it often.
explanation.definitionFit: A saga is a long story, originally a Norse heroic tale.

clue.text: Caught the engineers in engagements making extensions

indicators.note: in means placed inside what follows

blocks.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
engagements in battle are actions

explanation.surface: Army engineers trapped in battles while building additions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engagements' suggests betrothals, but here they are military clashes.
explanation.definitionFit: Accretions are additions built up gradually, growing something larger.

clue.text: Striking out the CIA(gency)

definitions.note: a whimsical second sense: catching 'eyes', i.e. spies, is outing the agency

blocks.note: first meaning: grabbing attention
second meaning: an eye is a detective or spy, so catching them exposes the agency

explanation.surface: Taking strike action against the American intelligence agency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striking' suggests industrial action; it is the plain definition. The bracketed 'gency' stresses that the CIA is an agency full of eyes, as in private eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Something eye-catching grabs attention, which is what a striking sight does.

clue.text: Gourmet enjoyed crushed ice with a prune

indicators.note: crushed things are broken up, so the letters are mashed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A food lover relished a dessert of crushed ice and a prune.
explanation.definitionFit: An epicurean is a person devoted to fine food and drink, a connoisseur of eating.

clue.text: Start a prison escape?

blocks.note: first meaning: a sudden beginning, as of a war or disease
second meaning: a breakout, read as breaking out of jail

explanation.surface: Planning the beginning of a jailbreak.
explanation.definitionFit: An outbreak is the sudden start of something, and a break out of prison is an escape.

clue.text: Horribly loud, noisy, nameless composition

indicators.note: nameless means without a name, so the abbreviation for name is dropped
a composition is something put together, so the letters are arranged afresh

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written; its N, the abbreviation for name, goes

explanation.surface: A review of a dreadful, deafening piece by an anonymous composer.
explanation.walkthrough: N is a standard abbreviation for name.
explanation.definitionFit: Odiously means in a hateful, repugnant way, which is horribly.

clue.text: He never gets a lot

blocks.note: surface: someone who is always short-changed
setter's reading: a lot is an item at auction, and this bidder is always outbid

explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot' means a large amount in the surface, but here it is an auction item.
explanation.definitionFit: At auction, the person making the second-highest bid loses the item to the winner.

clue.text: One who is inclined to be slimmer?

blocks.note: first meaning: someone who leans
second meaning: thinner, comparative adjective

explanation.surface: A dieter who wants to lose weight.
explanation.definitionFit: A leaner is one who tilts or leans, and leaner is also the comparative of lean, meaning thin.

clue.text: Averts chaos fast

indicators.note: chaos is complete disorder, so the letters fall into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone quickly heads off disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' looks like an adverb meaning quickly, but it is the verb meaning go without food.
explanation.definitionFit: To starve is to go without food, and to fast is to abstain from eating.

clue.text: Noise barrier

blocks.note: first meaning: a deep resonant sound
second meaning: a floating barrier across a harbour or river

explanation.surface: A wall built to block sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A boom is a loud deep sound, and also a floating beam blocking a waterway.

clue.text: A case for internal treatment? On the contrary

definitions.text: A case for internal treatment? On the contrary

blocks.note: surface: someone who needs to be admitted to hospital
setter's reading: reverse 'internal', so this case is treated externally, without a hospital stay

explanation.surface: A doctor deciding whether a patient needs admitting.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half describes an inpatient; 'On the contrary' flips in to its opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: This patient attends hospital for treatment without staying overnight, the opposite of an inpatient.

clue.text: Make representations for the French to occupy the flat

indicators.note: to occupy a place is to be inside it

blocks.note: a pad is slang for a flat or home
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A lobbying campaign for French tenants to take over an apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make representations' is the formal phrase for arguing a case to an authority.
explanation.definitionFit: To plead is to argue a case or appeal, to make representations on someone's behalf.

clue.text: Hard worker pulls up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: tows means pulls along

explanation.surface: A diligent worker who hauls things up.
explanation.walkthrough: A swot is British slang for a student who studies hard.
explanation.definitionFit: A swot is someone who works hard at their studies, a hard worker in the classroom.

clue.text: We''ll see her perhaps, having dropped a student in another place

indicators.note: perhaps hints the letters are only one possible arrangement, so they may be reshuffled
dropping something leaves it out

blocks.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe
L for learner, from the L-plate on a learner driver's car

explanation.surface: Someone expects to meet a woman after leaving a pupil somewhere else.
explanation.walkthrough: One of the two Ls goes, then the rest is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Elsewhere means somewhere other than here, in a different location.

clue.text: One who has now changed — but with some hesitation

indicators.note: changed means altered, so the letters are put in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
er is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: Someone who is a different person now, though still a little unsure.
explanation.definitionFit: An owner is a person who possesses something, someone who has it.

clue.text: Ronnie or Reggie lost a hundred at poker originally — what a gas!

indicators.note: something lost is gone, so a letter is taken away
originally points to the start, the first letter of the word before it

blocks.note: Ronnie and Reggie Kray were twin gangsters in 1960s London
taken as written; this letter is removed
first letter of poker
a ton is slang for a hundred

explanation.surface: A gangster loses a large sum at cards, and the exclamation says what fun it was.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A' does double work: it is the letter KRAY loses and the start of 'a hundred'. The Kray twins were notorious East End gangsters.
explanation.definitionFit: Krypton is a noble gas, element 36; 'what a gas!' also means 'what fun!'

clue.text: Be worthy of French opening shot

blocks.note: de is French for of
the serve is the first shot in a rally of tennis

explanation.surface: Praise for a French player's first stroke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Be worthy of' looks like the whole definition, but 'of' belongs with 'French'.
explanation.definitionFit: To deserve something is to merit it, to be entitled to it.
